meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 9: Doing Things (2): Do You Often Come Here? (Extras)
meta.baseChapterLabel: Lesson 9: Doing Things (2): Do You Often Come Here?

items.english: Yesterday, I sent an e-mail at the office.
items.target: きのうかいしゃでメールをおくりました
items.pronunciation: kinō kaisha de mēru o okurimashita
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [time] [place] で メールを おくりました. The lesson's メールをおくります family already has five source examples across で/に and tenses; this is one more variant of an already over-taught verb.

items.english: Emma-san will telephone a friend.
items.target: エマさんはともだちにでんわをします
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa tomodachi ni denwa o shimasu
items.note: Minimal pair with ともだちとでんわをします (tomodachi to denwa o shimasu): に (ni) marks the friend as the person the call is directed at, that is, the one being dialed.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Minimal pair, half 1 of 2: に (person an action is directed at, this lesson) vs と (person you do something together with, Lesson 6). Only the particle differs between the two cards.

items.english: Smith-san will send an e-mail to the office.
items.target: スミスさんはかいしゃにメールをおくります
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san wa kaisha ni mēru o okurimasu
items.note: Minimal pair with かいしゃでメールをおくります (kaisha de mēru o okurimasu): に (ni) marks the office as the receiver the e-mail is directed at, while で (de) would mark it as merely the place where the sending happens.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Minimal pair, half 1 of 2: に (recipient/destination of おくります, this lesson's Grammar 2) vs で (place of action, Lesson 8). Only the particle differs between the two cards.

items.english: Two wine glasses, please.
items.target: グラスをふたつください
items.pronunciation: gurasu o futatsu kudasai
items.hint: The word is グラス (gurasu), the stemware word, not コップ (koppu)
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for グラス (no sentence anywhere), in the Lesson 5 counter-order frame. Hint added because English 'glass' could otherwise produce the Lesson 5 word コップ.
items.note: グラス (gurasu) is a stemmed wine glass, distinct from the everyday tumbler コップ (koppu) from Lesson 5 — see グラス (gurasu) card.

items.english: What do you recommend today?
items.target: きょうのおすすめはなんですか
items.pronunciation: kyō no osusume wa nan desu ka
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 1, Suzuki's opening line きょうの おすすめは なんですか. Only the bare vocabulary item おすすめ was carded; the printed question itself is missing.

items.english: No, she doesn't watch them very often.
items.target: いいえ、あまりみません
items.pronunciation: iie, amari mimasen
items.scene: Answering whether Emma-san often watches movies
items.note: よく (yoku) from the question cannot simply be negated; the natural negative reply downgrades to あまり (amari) plus the negative みません (mimasen), as in the book's Exercise VII dialogues.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Frequency-adverb coverage: あまり in its Q&A answer slot (the deck's only あまり card is a standalone statement). Elliptical, so it carries a scene naming the question.

items.english: Does Kato-san sometimes play golf?
items.target: かとうさんはときどきゴルフをしますか
items.pronunciation: katō-san wa tokidoki gorufu o shimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Frequency-adverb coverage: ときどき in question form with a する-verb; the deck's only ときどき sentences are wave 1's elliptical answer and the forms-set statement, so this adds the question slot.

items.english: I'll buy three yogurts at the supermarket.
items.target: スーパーでヨーグルトをみっつかいます
items.pronunciation: sūpā de yōguruto o mittsu kaimasu

items.english: Suzuki-san, do you often come to this restaurant?
items.target: すずきさんはよくこのみせにきますか
items.pronunciation: suzuki-san wa yoku kono mise ni kimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's line すずきさんは よく この みせに きますか. This is the lesson's title question ('Do you often come here?') and it was never carded; only the Exercise IX variant about the Shibuya Library made it in.

items.english: No, he doesn't read them at all.
items.target: いいえ、ぜんぜんよみません
items.pronunciation: iie, zenzen yomimasen
items.scene: Answering whether Smith-san often reads books
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Frequency-adverb coverage: ぜんぜん in its Q&A answer slot, the negative counterpart to the existing card はい、よくよみます for the existing question スミスさんはよくほんをよみますか. Elliptical, so it carries a scene naming the question.

items.english: Sasaki-san's husband takes a walk in the park every morning.
items.target: ささきさんのごしゅじんはまいあさこうえんでさんぽをします
items.pronunciation: sasaki-san no goshujin wa maiasa kōen de sampo o shimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for ごしゅじん and まいあさ, both sentence-less; uses the book's own possessor ささきさんのごしゅじん from Word Power, in the Lesson 8 place-で activity frame.

items.english: How do you like Japan?
items.target: にほんはどうですか
items.pronunciation: nihon wa dō desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form coverage for どうですか, taught in this lesson but absent from the deck; present-tense slot, asking a newcomer's impression.
items.note: どう asks for an impression rather than a fact — what you think of something, not what state it is in. Compare どうでしたか (Lesson 11) for the same question in the past. The word is formally introduced in Lesson 11.

items.english: Whom will Smith-san send an e-mail to?
items.target: スミスさんはだれにメールをおくりますか
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san wa dare ni mēru o okurimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise III, part 2, example 1: スミスさんは だれに メールを おくりますか. The deck has the どこに (doko ni) version of this e-mail question but the printed だれに (dare ni) version was skipped.

items.english: Mr. Suzuki, right?
items.target: すずきさまですね
items.pronunciation: suzuki-sama desu ne
items.scene: A restaurant employee politely confirming the name of the customer who just arrived
items.note: The employee uses the extra-polite 〜さま (-sama) instead of 〜さん (-san) because they are addressing a customer.
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, restaurant employee's line すずきさまですね. The vocabulary items さま and すずきさま were carded but this printed sentence never was; it is the only usage example of the new honorific in the deck.

items.english: Emma-san often goes to the library.
items.target: エマさんはよくとしょかんにいきます
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa yoku toshokan ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form contrast set, card 1 of 4: fixed frame エマさんは…としょかんにいきます cycled through the four frequency adverbs; only the adverb changes.

items.english: As for last week, I didn't play tennis.
items.target: せんしゅうはテニスをしませんでした
items.pronunciation: senshū wa tenisu o shimasen deshita
items.note: Topical は (wa) on the time word plus the negative past ませんでした (masen deshita): the implied contrast is with weeks when the speaker does play.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle coverage for topical は on a time expression, negative-past slot; third genuinely different frame alongside wave 1's statement and the question card.

items.english: We would like to pay separately.
items.target: べつべつにおねがいします
items.pronunciation: betsubetsu ni onegaishimasu
items.note: べつべつで おねがいします (betsubetsu de onegaishimasu) is also used, per the lesson's notes.
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 2, Suzuki's line べつべつに おねがいします, which also gets its own NOTES entry in the book. Only the bare adverb べつべつに was carded; the printed expression is missing.

items.english: Emma-san does not go to the library at all.
items.target: エマさんはぜんぜんとしょかんにいきません
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa zenzen toshokan ni ikimasen
items.note: ぜんぜん (zenzen) also requires the negative verb, and is stronger than あまり (amari): not at all versus not much.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form contrast set, card 4 of 4: ぜんぜん with the mandatory negative, completing the よく/ときどき/あまり/ぜんぜん cycle on one fixed sentence.

items.english: My father goes to the office by car every morning.
items.target: ちちはまいあさくるまでかいしゃにいきます
items.pronunciation: chichi wa maiasa kuruma de kaisha ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [family] は くるまで かいしゃに いきます. Nearly identical to the source card v9-chichi-wa-kuruma-de, same subject (ちち) and same sentence with only まいあさ added.

items.english: Tanaka-san's wife is British.
items.target: たなかさんのおくさんはイギリスじんです
items.pronunciation: tanaka-san no okusan wa igirisujin desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for おくさん (no sentence anywhere); reuses the Lesson 1 nationality copula frame.

items.english: My husband goes to the gym every week.
items.target: おっとはまいしゅうジムにいきます
items.pronunciation: otto wa maishū jimu ni ikimasu
items.hint: 'My husband' here is おっと (otto), not しゅじん (shujin)
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for おっと (bare vocab card only). Collision: おっと and しゅじん both translate as 'my husband', so this card and v9-shujin-wa-nyusu each carry a hint naming which synonym to produce.
items.note: おっと (otto) and しゅじん (shujin) are two readings of the same word for 'my husband' — see おっと (otto) card. This sentence uses おっと.

items.english: He will meet Suzuki-san.
items.target: すずきさんにあいます
items.pronunciation: suzuki-san ni aimasu
items.scene: Answering the question of whom Smith-san will meet tomorrow
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle coverage: elliptical answer to p9-ashita-dare-ni-aimasu-ka, keeping に (ni) plus verb in the reply as the book's drill answers do. Elliptical, so it carries a scene naming the question.

items.english: Emma-san sometimes goes to the library.
items.target: エマさんはときどきとしょかんにいきます
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa tokidoki toshokan ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form contrast set, card 2 of 4: same fixed frame, ときどき still with the affirmative verb.

items.english: Emma-san drinks vegetable juice every morning.
items.target: エマさんはまいあさやさいジュースをのみます
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa maiasa yasai jūsu o nomimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for やさいジュース (no sentence anywhere), in the habitual-present frame from this lesson's Grammar 3, matching the book's Exercise VI material.

items.english: Yes, I come sometimes.
items.target: ええ、ときどききます
items.pronunciation: ē, tokidoki kimasu
items.scene: Answering whether you often come to this restaurant
items.hint: Uses the softer ええ (ē) for 'yes', as in the dialogue
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Suzuki's reply ええ、ときどき きます. The frequency adverb ときどき is carded only as bare vocabulary; this is the book's printed answer to the title question and was never carded. Hint added because 'yes' would otherwise produce はい (hai).
items.note: ええ (ē) is a softer, more casual 'yes' than はい (hai) — natural in relaxed conversation with restaurant staff you know.

items.english: I don't eat vegetables very often.
items.target: あまりやさいをたべません
items.pronunciation: amari yasai o tabemasen
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for やさい (no sentence anywhere); doubles as a third あまり example in a first-person eating frame, respecting the mandatory negative.

items.english: As for tomorrow, where will you go?
items.target: あしたはどこにいきますか
items.pronunciation: ashita wa doko ni ikimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle coverage for topical は on a time expression, question-form slot (the index's どこにいきますか cards all use bare time words with no は).

items.english: And something to drink?
items.target: おのみものは
items.pronunciation: onomimono wa
items.scene: A server taking a food order, asking what the customer would like to drink
items.hint: Elliptical question ending in は (wa): literally 'as for a drink…?'
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 1, the employee's line おのみものは?. Only the vocabulary item おのみもの was carded; this printed elliptical question was skipped.
items.note: おのみものは trails off with は (wa), the same ellipsis as Lesson 8's ささきさんは (sasaki-san wa) — the rest ('would you like?') is dropped as understood.

items.english: Two draft beers, please.
items.target: なまビールを２つおねがいします
items.pronunciation: nama bīru o futatsu onegaishimasu
items.ttsText: なまビールをふたつおねがいします
items.hint: Draft beer, ordered with the general counter
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 1, Suzuki's line なまビールを ２つ おねがいします. Only the vocabulary item なまビール was carded. Hint added because the existing card ビールを２ほんおねがいします ('Two bottles of beer, please.') has a very close English gloss.
items.note: Draft beer takes the general counter つ (tsu), not the long-object counter ほん (hon) used for bottled beer in ビールを２ほんおねがいします — it's measured by glass, not by bottle.

items.english: It's this one.
items.target: こちらです
items.pronunciation: kochira desu
items.scene: A restaurant employee answering what today's recommendation is, while politely presenting it
items.note: こちら (kochira) is the polite service-register word for これ (kore).
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 1, the employee's reply こちらです. The chapter glosses こちら as the polite word for これ but no card demonstrates it. Elliptical answer, so it carries a scene naming the question.

items.english: Last week, I met Suzuki-san's wife.
items.target: せんしゅうすずきさんのおくさんにあいました
items.pronunciation: senshū suzuki-san no okusan ni aimashita
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [time] [person]の[family] に あいました. Near-duplicate of v9-gokazoku-ni-aimashita (きのうたなかさんのごかぞくにあいました), and the あいます verb is already drilled across several other source cards.

items.english: Does Emma-san often watch movies?
items.target: エマさんはよくえいがをみますか
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa yoku eiga o mimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Frequency-adverb coverage: よく question with a を-verb (existing よく questions all use motion or よみます); paired with the あまり answer card that follows.

items.english: Smith-san and Suzuki-san met Green-san at the tempura restaurant in Ginza.
items.target: スミスさんとすずきさんはぎんざのてんぷらやでグリーンさんにあいました
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san to suzuki-san wa ginza no tempuraya de gurīn-san ni aimashita
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue closing summary sentence スミスさんと すずきさんは ぎんざの てんぷらやで グリーンさんに あいました. It is the only printed sentence using the new word てんぷらや and was never carded.

items.english: How was the trip?
items.target: りょこうはどうでしたか
items.pronunciation: ryokō wa dō deshita ka
items.note: でしたか (deshita ka) is the past of ですか (desu ka), so this asks for an impression after the trip is over.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form coverage for どうですか in its past form どうでしたか, pairing with f9-nihon-wa-do-desu-ka to show the present/past contrast on the same pattern.

items.english: School is from 9:00 to 3:00.
items.target: がっこうは９じから３じまでです
items.pronunciation: gakkō wa kuji kara sanji made desu
items.ttsText: がっこうはくじからさんじまでです
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for がっこう, which appears in no sentence; reuses the Lesson 3 から/まで hours frame instead of another motion sentence. Numerals in target, so a kana reading is supplied.

items.english: Excuse me, could we have the bill separately, please?
items.target: すみません。おかいけいをべつべつにおねがいします
items.pronunciation: sumimasen. okaikei o betsubetsu ni onegaishimasu
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: すみません。おかいけいを[adverb]におねがいします. Just recombines two phrases the source already teaches separately (ex9-okaikei-o-onegaishimasu and ex9-betsubetsu-ni-onegaishimasu) in an already heavily-drilled おねがいします pattern.

items.english: My father goes to the office by car.
items.target: ちちはくるまでかいしゃにいきます
items.pronunciation: chichi wa kuruma de kaisha ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for ちち (no sentence anywhere); reuses the Lesson 7 means-of-transport frame.

items.english: Excuse me. May we have the bill, please?
items.target: すみません。おかいけいをおねがいします
items.pronunciation: sumimasen. okaikei o onegaishimasu
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 2, Suzuki's line すみません。おかいけいを おねがいします. Only the vocabulary item おかいけい was carded; the printed bill-request sentence itself is missing.

items.english: It's a nice restaurant, isn't it?
items.target: いいみせですね
items.pronunciation: ii mise desu ne
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's line いい みせですね. The new adjective いい (ii, 'nice, good') appears in the chapter vocabulary but no card uses it; this printed sentence was skipped entirely. PRE-EXCLUDED: the reviewer excluded いい (ii) from the base lesson as premature (formally taught in Lesson 10) — restore this card if early exposure inside the book's own printed sentence is wanted.

items.english: Suzuki-san always returns home at 7:00.
items.target: すずきさんはいつも７じにうちにかえります
items.pronunciation: suzuki-san wa itsumo shichiji ni uchi ni kaerimasu
items.ttsText: すずきさんはいつもしちじにうちにかえります
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for いつも, which appears in no sentence; combined with the Lesson 7 time-に + かえります frame. Numeral in target, so a kana reading is supplied.

items.english: I met Tanaka-san's family yesterday.
items.target: きのうたなかさんのごかぞくにあいました
items.pronunciation: kinō tanaka-san no gokazoku ni aimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for ごかぞく (and the honorific prefix ご), which appears in no sentence; delivered in the new に+あいます frame.

items.english: Emma-san will talk on the phone with a friend.
items.target: エマさんはともだちとでんわをします
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa tomodachi to denwa o shimasu
items.note: Minimal pair with ともだちにでんわをします (tomodachi ni denwa o shimasu): と (to, 'together with', Lesson 6) makes the friend the partner sharing the phone conversation, not the person being dialed, which would take に (ni).
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Minimal pair, half 2 of 2: と (companion) vs に (receiver of the action). Only the particle differs between the two cards.

items.english: Please tell me the location of Restaurant Rome.
items.target: レストランローマのばしょをおしえてください
items.pronunciation: resutoran rōma no basho o oshiete kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for レストランローマ (no sentence anywhere); reuses the Lesson 2 おしえてください request frame combined with this lesson's ばしょ.

items.english: I'll eat at home.
items.target: うちでたべます
items.pronunciation: uchi de tabemasu

items.english: Where will Smith-san telephone?
items.target: スミスさんはどこにでんわをしますか
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san wa doko ni denwa o shimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise III, example 2 of the telephone dialogues: スミスさんは どこに でんわを しますか. The deck carded the だれに (dare ni) telephone question and the どこに (doko ni) e-mail question but skipped this どこに telephone example.

items.english: Where will you eat dinner?
items.target: ばんごはんはどこでたべますか
items.pronunciation: bangohan wa doko de tabemasu ka

items.english: On Sunday, Emma-san went to the department store with her mother.
items.target: エマさんはにちようびにおかあさんとデパートにいきました
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa nichiyōbi ni okāsan to depāto ni ikimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for おかあさん (no sentence anywhere); reuses the Lesson 6/7 companion-と motion frame rather than this chapter's phone frame, for variety.

items.english: Emma-san does not go to the library very often.
items.target: エマさんはあまりとしょかんにいきません
items.pronunciation: ema-san wa amari toshokan ni ikimasen
items.note: あまり (amari) cannot stand with the affirmative いきます (ikimasu); it forces the negative いきません (ikimasen).
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form contrast set, card 3 of 4: the verb flips to the negative because of あまり, this lesson's Grammar 4.

items.english: Smith-san will send an e-mail at the office.
items.target: スミスさんはかいしゃでメールをおくります
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san wa kaisha de mēru o okurimasu
items.note: Minimal pair with かいしゃにメールをおくります (kaisha ni mēru o okurimasu): で (de) marks the office as the place where the sending is done, and the recipient goes unstated. With に (ni) the office itself would be the receiver.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Minimal pair, half 2 of 2: で (place of action) vs に (recipient). Only the particle differs between the two cards.

items.english: As for today, I'm eating dinner at home.
items.target: きょうはうちでばんごはんをたべます
items.pronunciation: kyō wa uchi de bangohan o tabemasu
items.note: The は (wa) after きょう (kyō) makes today the topic and implies contrast with other days, the same use as せんしゅうは (senshū wa) in this lesson's Target Dialogue.
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle coverage for topical は on a time expression, this lesson's NOTES point; only wave 1's せんしゅうは card exists. Affirmative statement slot.

items.english: My husband watches the news every evening.
items.target: しゅじんはまいばんニュースをみます
items.pronunciation: shujin wa maiban nyūsu o mimasu
items.hint: 'My husband' here is しゅじん (shujin), not おっと (otto)
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for しゅじん (the book's alternative to おっと, in no card at all) and for まいばん, also sentence-less. Collision with v9-otto-wa-jimu over 'my husband', hence the hint on each.
items.note: しゅじん (shujin) and おっと (otto) are two readings of the same word for 'my husband' — see おっと (otto) card. This sentence uses しゅじん.

items.english: I sent my mother an e-mail yesterday.
items.target: きのうははにメールをおくりました
items.pronunciation: kinō haha ni mēru o okurimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for はは (no sentence anywhere); delivered in this lesson's recipient-に e-mail frame, past tense for variety.

items.english: I often buy yogurt at the supermarket.
items.target: よくスーパーでヨーグルトをかいます
items.pronunciation: yoku sūpā de yōguruto o kaimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for ヨーグルト (no sentence anywhere); the buy-at frame plus よく also adds another frequency-adverb slot.

items.english: I'll send an e-mail to a friend.
items.target: ともだちにメールをおくります
items.pronunciation: tomodachi ni mēru o okurimasu
items.note: に marks the recipient of the e-mail here, not a location.
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [person] に (メールを) おくります. The source already drills this frame repeatedly (だれにメールをおくりますか, なかむらさんにおくります, ははにメールをおくりました, かいしゃにメールをおくります), so another noun-swap adds nothing.

items.english: Suzuki-san teaches Emma-san Japanese.
items.target: すずきさんはエマさんににほんごをおしえます
items.pronunciation: suzuki-san wa ema-san ni nihongo o oshiemasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Double duty: particle coverage for に with おしえます in the teach-a-skill slot (existing cards only use the tell-information slot with でんわばんごう/ばしょ), and vocabulary coverage for にほんご, which appears in no sentence.

items.english: Whom will Smith-san meet tomorrow?
items.target: スミスさんはあしただれにあいますか
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san wa ashita dare ni aimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle coverage: に with あいます exists only in statements (index KS1/KS5, wave 1); this supplies the missing question form, mirroring the drill pattern だれに (dare ni).

items.english: I teach Japanese at school.
items.target: がっこうでにほんごをおしえます
items.pronunciation: gakkō de nihongo o oshiemasu
items.note: で here marks the place of teaching, unlike に which marked the student in the earlier example.

items.english: My wife sometimes goes shopping in Shibuya.
items.target: かないはときどきしぶやでかいものをします
items.pronunciation: kanai wa tokidoki shibuya de kaimono o shimasu
items.hint: 'My wife' here is かない (kanai), not つま (tsuma)
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for かない, the book's alternative to つま, which appears in no card at all; also adds a ときどき statement slot. Collision with v9-tsuma-to-kabuki over 'my wife', hence the hint on each.
items.note: つま (tsuma) and かない (kanai) are two readings of the same word for 'my wife' — see つま (tsuma) card. This sentence uses かない.

items.english: Last week, I met Green-san here.
items.target: せんしゅうはここでグリーンさんにあいました
items.pronunciation: senshū wa koko de gurīn-san ni aimashita
items.note: The は (wa) after せんしゅう (senshū) singles out last week as the topic from among the times the speaker has come here, as explained in the lesson's notes.
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Suzuki's line せんしゅうは ここで グリーンさんに あいました, also the subject of the lesson's NOTES section on topical は. It combines new に + あいます with ここ and was never carded.

items.english: Smith-san asked Tanaka-san the location of the meeting.
items.target: スミスさんはたなかさんにかいぎのばしょをききました
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san wa tanaka-san ni kaigi no basho o kikimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle coverage: に with ききます (ask) has exactly one sentence in the deck (でんわばんごうをききました); this varies the thing asked about (ばしょ) and the people.

items.english: Well then, we'll have two of those, please.
items.target: じゃ、それを２つおねがいします
items.pronunciation: ja, sore o futatsu onegaishimasu
items.ttsText: じゃ、それをふたつおねがいします
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 1, Suzuki's line じゃ、それを ２つ おねがいします. The deck's closest cards use ください with counters (Lesson 5); this printed ordering line with おねがいします plus the general counter was never carded.

items.english: Yesterday I saw kabuki with my wife.
items.target: きのうつまとかぶきをみました
items.pronunciation: kinō tsuma to kabuki o mimashita
items.hint: 'My wife' here is つま (tsuma), not かない (kanai)
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for つま (bare vocab card only, no sentence). Collision: つま and かない both translate as 'my wife', so this card and v9-kanai-wa-kaimono each carry a hint naming which synonym to produce.
items.note: つま (tsuma) and かない (kanai) are two readings of the same word for 'my wife' — see つま (tsuma) card. This sentence uses つま.

items.english: He'll send it to Nakamura-san.
items.target: なかむらさんにおくります
items.pronunciation: nakamura-san ni okurimasu
items.scene: Answering whom Smith-san will send an e-mail to
items.reviewNote: Exercise III, part 2, example 1 reply なかむらさんに おくります. The telephone counterpart なかむらさんにします is carded; this printed e-mail reply is not. Elliptical answer, so it carries a scene naming the question.

items.english: The company president is going to the Sapporo branch next week.
items.target: しゃちょうはらいしゅうさっぽろししゃにいきます
items.pronunciation: shachō wa raishū sapporo shisha ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for しゃちょう and さっぽろししゃ, both sentence-less; reuses the Lesson 6 destination frame with a future time word.

items.english: It is 7:00 A.M. in Rome now.
items.target: ローマはいまごぜん７じです
items.pronunciation: rōma wa ima gozen shichiji desu
items.ttsText: ローマはいまごぜんしちじです
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for ローマ (no sentence anywhere); reuses the Lesson 3 world-clock frame (とうきょうはいまごごよじはんです). Numeral in target, so a kana reading is supplied.

items.english: Suzuki-san telephones his father every week.
items.target: すずきさんはまいしゅうおとうさんにでんわをします
items.pronunciation: suzuki-san wa maishū otōsan ni denwa o shimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for おとうさん and まいしゅう, both sentence-less; uses the drill A frame (person に でんわをします) plus a habitual time word, per this lesson's Grammar 3.

items.english: He'll call the bank.
items.target: ぎんこうにします
items.pronunciation: ginkō ni shimasu
items.hint: The reply keeps only します (shimasu), short for でんわをします (denwa o shimasu)
items.reviewNote: Exercise III, example 2 reply ぎんこうに します. Its e-mail counterpart ぎんこうにおくります is already carded but this telephone reply is not. Elliptical answer, so it carries a scene naming the question.
items.note: ぎんこうにします is short for ぎんこうにでんわをします — the reply drops でんわを (denwa o) since the question already established 'telephone' as the activity.

items.english: Suzuki-san drank beer in Sapporo.
items.target: すずきさんはさっぽろでビールをのみました
items.pronunciation: suzuki-san wa sapporo de bīru o nomimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary coverage for さっぽろ as a standalone place name (only さっぽろししゃ is otherwise covered); uses the Lesson 8 place-で past frame.

items.english: Drink
items.target: のみもの
items.pronunciation: nomimono
items.note: The noun built from のみます (nomimasu) 'to drink'. A restaurant says it with the polite お (o): おのみもの (onomimono).
items.hint: the noun, a thing you drink
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 9 already teaches nomimono. Needs a hint on merge, because the English gloss "Drink" also reaches のみます (nomimasu), the verb: "the noun, a thing you drink". The book card nomimasu (chapter-8) takes "the verb, what you do with a drink".

items.english: I eat vegetables.
items.target: やさいをたべます
items.pronunciation: yasai o tabemasu
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: yasai is taught in Lesson 9

items.english: A recommended restaurant
items.target: おすすめのみせ
items.pronunciation: osusume no mise
items.note: おすすめ (osusume) from this lesson, joined to みせ (mise) with の (no).
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: puts this lesson's おすすめ (osusume) into a phrase rather than leaving it a bare noun.

items.english: I study Japanese.
items.target: にほんごをべんきょうします
items.pronunciation: nihongo o benkyō shimasu
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the only sentence にほんご (nihongo), taught bare in this lesson, appears in.

items.english: Italian (the language)
items.target: イタリアご
items.pronunciation: itariago
items.note: The ご (go) suffix turns a country into its language, the same way にほん (nihon) becomes にほんご (nihongo).
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: shows ご (go) is a productive suffix, not part of the fixed word にほんご (nihongo).

items.english: English (the language)
items.target: えいご
items.pronunciation: eigo
items.note: Irregular against the pattern: it is えいご (eigo), not イギリスご (igirisugo), even though the country is イギリス (igirisu).
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the exception to the ご (go) suffix pattern, which is where a learner silently goes wrong.

items.english: Every Monday
items.target: まいしゅうげつようび
items.pronunciation: maishū getsuyōbi
items.note: まいしゅう (maishū) 'every week' in front of a day names that day every week.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: combines this lesson's まいしゅう (maishū) with a weekday from Lesson 7.

items.english: What time do you get up every day?
items.target: まいにち、なんじにおきますか
items.pronunciation: mainichi nan-ji ni okimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 1. Job: this lesson's まいにち (mainichi) with a habitual verb, plus the に (ni) that marks a clock time.

items.english: I get up at eight o'clock.
items.target: わたしは、はちじにおきます
items.pronunciation: watashi wa hachi-ji ni okimasu
items.scene: answering what time you get up
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 1 answer. Job: the second of the two sentences おきます (okimasu) appears in.

items.english: How did you come here today?
items.target: きょう、どうやってここにきましたか
items.pronunciation: kyō dō yatte koko ni kimashita ka
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 6. Job: どうやって (dō yatte) in the past, on this lesson's ここ (koko).

items.english: I came here by train.
items.target: でんしゃでここにきました
items.pronunciation: densha de koko ni kimashita
items.scene: answering how you got here today
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 6 answer. Job: the で (de) of means answering a どうやって (dō yatte) question in the past.

items.english: What time did you go to bed last night?
items.target: さくばん、なんじにねましたか
items.pronunciation: sakuban nan-ji ni nemashita ka
items.note: さくばん (sakuban) is last night. きのうのよる (kinō no yoru) says the same thing more plainly.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 7. Job: the past of the なんじに (nan-ji ni) time question, against the present-tense one above.

items.english: I went to bed at twelve.
items.target: じゅうにじにねました
items.pronunciation: jūni-ji ni nemashita
items.scene: answering what time you went to bed
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 7 answer. Job: the second of the two sentences ねました (nemashita) appears in.
